text: In contrast to neutrophils, research indicates a potential role for macrophages in regenerative processes following EIMD (277), and some researchers even speculate that they are necessary for muscle growth (131). Macrophages appear to exert anabolic effects by secreting local growth factors associated with inflammatory processes. Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), a myokine considered crucial for overload-induced hypertrophy, is thought to play a particularly important role in the process. Following muscle injury, VEGF acts as a chemoattractant for macrophages, initiating the inflammatory response and release of IGF-1, among other anabolic agents (120).
